lines: Finding the right work is harder when everyone asks if you found it yet.
Work is work. Finding the right work is the tricky part.
Waiting for work is still work if you look worried enough.
Where do I fit? Somewhere useful, I hope, preferably before supper.
People with trades get tasks. People without trades get errands.
A fair chance is easier to ask for than to recognize.
A fair chance can look a lot like standing around until the right bell rings.
I once followed the bell hoping it meant opportunity. It meant hurry.
I organized a barrel once. For a moment, everyone thought I had a calling.
If you see a spare job site, do mention it kindly.
Give the job site I have not found yet room. Looking useful works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the job site I have not found yet. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
Unemployed jokes are flexible. That is what I keep telling myself.
Looking useful jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with time on them.
I keep a spare joke near the job site I have not found yet. It is not always ready for public use.
That was idle talk, and I would know.
I have seen wrong turns with more sense than that.
Careful. Even time looks softer than your manners right now.
I am trying to look useful, not involved.
Keep your voice even. I am measuring more than your words.
Some questions are safer when they stand a little farther away.
I remember having no trade, no thoughts, almost no self. You helped with the important one.
I did not know what I would become, but you made sure I could become anything.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
Your face is familiar. So is being confused, but this feels different.
I remember waking with empty hands and a head full of broken bells.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
I remember you, though I still do not know what to do with the memory.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Thunder shook the village square so hard every loose shutter complained, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked beds, doors, and loose chores after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the village square, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked who still needed help.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have neighbors to check on.
I checked roofs, beds, and unlucky fences for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the water bucket after.
Odd jobs can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the village square, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the village square, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, odd jobs can wait; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the village square still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before beds, doors, and loose chores. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the village square and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the edge of the square, I saw fear run through the village; then I saw courage catch up.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the village square first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the gap between torches and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the village square enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping a ready pair of hands between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the village square, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning dust from the doorways.
I checked beds, doors, and loose chores, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand reached the village square, the hinges, and half our eyes, but no one has been reported missing.
A hard wind teaches a villager which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough near the village square, though the whole village sounds like it is chewing gravel.
Odd jobs can wait. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the village square found shelter.
Cold works quietly around the village square. We are checking on anyone who stayed quiet too long.
I am clearing snow from the meeting path and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now near the village square. Keep the fires fed and the paths open.
I do not have a trade for it yet, but coming home safely feels like honest work.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I will count that as good work.
I was looking for direction, not bruises. Still, I made it back.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
I followed because I thought you knew where we were going. I was wrong about more than the road.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
I learned I am not ready for a career in boating. But I survived the lesson.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
I followed you once and learned something: I need better shoes before I choose a trade.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
I followed you into a boat once. Not a trade, apparently, but it felt like training.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
It helped. Maybe being ready is a profession of its own for now.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
Unused so far. I may not have a trade, but I know preparation when I see it.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
I am still finding my place here. You made sure there was a here to find it in.
I had no station, no trade, just a door to hide behind. You kept that door standing.
I do not have much here yet, but you helped keep what I might become part of.
The village still has room for me because people like you fought for it.
I had nowhere important to stand, so I watched. You stood somewhere important.
You protected more than houses. You protected chances.
I saw a future here look less certain, then you pushed back.
Maybe I will find work tomorrow because there is still a village tomorrow.
I am trying to belong here. Please do not make that harder.
Fine. We can start again from here, but not from before.
I am still figuring out where I fit. Please do not make me fit around fear.
Fine. I accept, but I need room to believe it.
That helps. Not everything, but it helps.
I do not have a profession for judging apologies. This one sounds real enough to start.
Let us call this a beginning, not a finish.
I will give the apology a place. Give me a reason to keep it there.
I do not have a trade for that sort of night. I survived it anyway.
I found a corner, then a path, then home. That is more plan than I started with.
I made it back without a trade, a plan, or much dignity. Still counts.
I learned that I am very motivated by closed doors and warm lights.
Home looked like the best job I could possibly have.
I survived by following people who seemed less confused than I was.
I reached the village and decided that was enough achievement for the day.
I have no title for what I did. I lived through it.
Take {gift_item}. I may not have a trade, but I know how to say thanks.
Here, {gift_item}. Maybe one of us will find the perfect use for it.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
Good, {gift_item} worked. See? I can be useful without a workstation.
{tested_villager} liked it? Excellent. I am putting that under possible talents.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}; I like advice that holds up.
Ah. Then my career in advice pauses here. Try {alternative_gift} for {gift_subject}.
{gift_item} was wrong? Let us call it research. {alternative_gift} should work better.
{gift_item} missed the mark for {gift_subject}. Try {alternative_gift} instead.
This is why nobody pays me for advice. Try {alternative_gift}.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess: {alternative_gift} next time.
You came back? Fair. My next guess is {alternative_gift}.
Set {gift_item} aside and try {alternative_gift}. This advice should land better.
Then we correct the guess: {alternative_gift} next time.
Mind the job site I have not found yet. What do you need?
Step clear of the job site I have not found yet. What do you need?
Mind the job site I have not found yet; I am listening.
Back to looking useful before anyone notices, then.
Back to looking useful before the work notices I stopped.
I have chance to tend and daylight to spend.
Fine. I have enough problems without carrying this one too.
Fine. I will set this down before it gets heavier.
Fine. I can step back, but do not make me regret it.
Even without a trade, I know that should be {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
That is short of the full repair. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
Not enough. It takes {emerald_cost} {emeralds} to settle this.
No. I may not have work, but I still have sense.
No. Some damage has to cool before payment matters.
No. Keep {payment_items}; trust is not ready to trade.
